title: A flow-cytometry-based protocol using diverse cell types for detecting autoantibodies from human plasma and serum samples
protocol: Aspirate expended media from culture vessels.
Wash cells once with ambient temperature PBS.
Swirl flask carefully ensuring the cellular monolayer makes thorough contact with the PBS.
Aspirate the PBS.
Dissociate subconfluent (<85%) target cells from T-175 culture flasks by adding 5 mL undiluted TrypLE Express reagent or an alternate dissociating reagent following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer flasks to a 37°C incubator.
Check flasks periodically for cell detachment.
Collect cells with 40 mL cold PBS and run through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new sterile 50 mL tube.
Fill the tube containing cells with cold PBS.
Spin cells down at 500 × g for 3 min.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 5.0 × 10^5 cells/mL in cold PBS.
Dispense 100 μL into each well of a U-bottom 96 well plate (5.0 × 10^4 cells/well).
Work with plates on a bed of ice to maintain high cell viability.
Ascertain cell viability through automated counting methods or manually using trypan blue exclusion.
Ensure cell viabilities are greater than 90% for accurate results.
Return cells to culture and reattempt experiments if cell viabilities are lower than 90%.
Designate a row within a plate as controls, followed by sample rows.
Cells in the control wells will not be used to screen biological samples.
The IgG Positive control well receives both the anti-CD98 antibody and the staining cocktail.
Single color controls provide preliminary guidance for positive-event gates along with unstained controls.
Refine gate placements using boundaries set by fluorescence-minus-one controls.
Transfer up to 50 μL of biological sample from the prepared sample plate to corresponding wells containing target cells.
Add 48 μL PBS and 2 μL anti-CD98 antibody (20 μg/mL final concentration) to one control well.
Ensure the final volume per well is 150 μL.
Mix samples gently by pipetting.
Transfer plates to 4°C for one hour.
Prepare a cell staining mastermix using PBS as a diluent while plates are incubating.
Include stains for other cellular markers as a means of providing assurances of cellular phenotype and/or cell health following culture.
As controls, include single-color stains and fluorescence-minus-one reactions performed in the absence of patient samples.
Prepare single-color stain controls by adding only secondary anti-Ig antibody stains to cells that have not been exposed to patient samples.
For fluorescence-minus-one control stains, add two anti-Ig antibodies but omit the third.
Retrieve plates containing cells from 4°C.
Top each well with 100 μL of cold PBS and spin down at 500 × g for 3 min.
Aspirate supernatants.
Wash cells once with 200 μL of cold PBS and repeat spin.
Aspirate supernatants and add mastermixes to all wells except for wells designated for no-stain, single-color and fluorescence-minus-one reactions.
Maintain well volumes to 100 μL by adding the appropriate volume of mastermix or other solutions.
Gently mix by pipetting.
Return plates to 4°C, in the dark, for 30 min.
Prepare a 1% (v/v) PFA solution by diluting PFA from stock in PBS and store on ice.
Retrieve cells from 4°C and top up with 100 μL of cold PBS.
Spin plates at 500 × g for 3 min.
Wash cells two more times in cold PBS, centrifuging cells at 500 × g for 3 min between each wash.
Aspirate PBS and fix cells with 100 μL 1% PFA.
Resuspend cells gently by pipetting.
Store plates at 4°C for up to three hours prior to acquisition if necessary.
Record as many events as possible on a flow cytometer.
Ensure height and width parameters on side and forward scatter are recorded.
Select fluorophores that minimally fluoresce at wavelengths of light used by others within the same antibody panel.
Utilize non-fluorescent beads (BD CompBeads Anti-Mouse Ig or ArC Amine reactive compensation beads) for performing compensation.
Substitute incompatible reagents with murine isotype control antibodies conjugated to the same fluorophore.
Ensure a main cellular population can be determined in Forward Vs. Side scatter.
Draw Forward scatter thresholds to eliminate background ‘noise’ events while leaving the main cellular population untouched.
Draw a gate capturing the main cellular population and use it as a stopping gate.
Record at least 5000 events, or until IgM, IgA, and/or IgG signals have stabilized, whichever is higher.
Identify the cellular population in the Forward Vs. Side scatter area plot.
Draw a gate in the Forward scatter (Area) Vs. Forward scatter (Height) plot to identify single events based on proportional Area and Height signals.
Select live cells based on viability dye staining.
Use single-color controls to define negative populations for events positive for Ig staining.
Refine gates based on the fluorescence-minus-one controls.
Apply these gating strategies to the samples.
